capture.final_message:
Split the conjunction.

- For the subgroup statement, use that scalar multiplication by \(a\) is an order automorphism of the subgroup lattice, with inverse scalar multiplication by \(a^{-1}\). Thus
  \[
  S\le a\!\cdot T \iff a^{-1}\!\cdot S\le a^{-1}\!\cdot(a\!\cdot T)=T.
  \]
  This should follow from the pointwise-action order equivalence, or elementwise using the group-action identities.

- For the permutation statement, use \(2<\operatorname{ncard}(s)\) to choose three distinct elements \(x,y,z\in s\). Let \(g\) be the 3-cycle \(x\mapsto y\mapsto z\mapsto x\), fixing everything else (constructed directly or from two transpositions). Then \(g\) is a three-cycle, and it preserves \(s\): it only permutes three elements already in \(s\) and fixes all other elements. Hence \(g\cdot s=s\), so \(g\) belongs to the stabilizer of \(s\).

The essential assumption is \(\operatorname{ncard}(s)>2\), precisely what supplies the three distinct points needed for the cycle.
